clue.text: Disputed mensurable territory claimed by occupiers?

indicators.note: a disputed claim is contested and unsettled, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Land whose measurement is contested is grabbed by an invading army.
explanation.walkthrough: LEBENSRAUM, German for 'living space', was the Nazi justification for seizing land to the east; the question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The German term names the extra living space a nation claims it needs, used as a pretext for conquest and occupation.

clue.text: Flipping old character embracing old mother in entrance

indicators.note: flipping turns the whole assembly over, so it is read from the end back
the old character wraps its arms round the next pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a rune is a letter of an ancient Germanic alphabet
Ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: An ancient script, flipped, contains a reference to an old mother at a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like a noun meaning a doorway, but it is the verb, stressed on the second syllable: to put in a trance.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to charm and captivate them, which is what it means to make them fall in love.

clue.text: County town has demolished church compound

indicators.note: the town has knocked down its church, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: Chester is the county town of Cheshire, its administrative centre

explanation.surface: A county town has knocked down one of its churches.
explanation.walkthrough: A county town is the administrative seat of an English county; Chester serves Cheshire.
explanation.definitionFit: An ester is an organic chemical compound formed when an acid reacts with an alcohol.

clue.text: Loans suspended mostly? Not so fast

parts.note: subs are advances of money, small loans against wages

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all of the phrase is kept, losing its final letter

parts.note: a plan that is suspended is put on ice

explanation.surface: A lender halts most of its loans and someone urges caution: not so fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not so fast' reads as a command to slow down, but it describes speed below that of sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsonic flight is slower than the speed of sound, so the aircraft is literally not so fast.

clue.text: English occultist reanimated 12 wearily

indicators.note: brought back to life in a new form, so the letters are given a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the answer to 12 across is used as letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dead magician is raised from the grave and returns tired.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference supplies a whole word: 12 across, combined with 'wearily', makes up all the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleister Crowley was a notorious early twentieth-century British magician and founder of the Thelema religion.

clue.text: After gender reassignment monkey becomes mean

indicators.note: the letter for female is swapped for the letter for male

parts.note: to monkey with something is to fiddle with it

explanation.surface: A monkey's gender is changed and it turns nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' tempts as unkind; here it is the average, the middle value. F for female becomes M for male.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle point between extremes is a mean, as in 'the golden mean'.

clue.text: Time for Iftar snack

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a particular day of the calendar
second meaning: the fruit traditionally eaten to break the Ramadan fast at sunset

explanation.walkthrough: Iftar is the meal Muslims eat at sunset during Ramadan, customarily begun with this fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a calendar day and the sweet fruit of the palm tree.

clue.text: Chap tired out? Not at all dear!

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exhausted man is told, kindly, that he is not at all dear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' looks like an endearment but means expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extremely inexpensive costs very little, the opposite of pricey.

clue.text: Doctor on Circle Line gets stuck in to a game of chance

indicators.note: the doctor, circle and line are pushed inside the two little words that follow

parts.note: taken as written
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine degree
a circle has the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A doctor riding London's Circle Line throws himself into a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route, but here circle and line are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a lottery, typically at a fete, where tickets are drawn from a revolving drum.

clue.text: Hypocrisy of actors after change of direction

indicators.note: one compass point, south, is swapped for another, north

parts.note: the actors in a play make up its cast

explanation.surface: Actors who change their tune are accused of hypocrisy.
explanation.walkthrough: S and N are the compass points south and north.
explanation.definitionFit: Cant is insincere, sanctimonious talk, pious language used without real belief.

clue.text: Cash given to underground cartoonist for a little food

parts.note: bread is slang for money
Robert Crumb was a leading artist of 1960s underground comix

explanation.surface: Money is handed to a subversive comic-strip artist so he can buy something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underground' suggests the Tube; it is the countercultural comics movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny fragment of bread is a small morsel of food.

clue.text: Judge rings about ballot box hack

indicators.note: the rings sit around the ballot box, enclosing it

parts.note: two rings, each the shape of the letter O
votes are traditionally cast into an urn

explanation.surface: A judge surrounds a ballot box during an election computer hack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' suggests breaking into a system; here it is a newspaper writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal, slightly disparaging words for a journalist.

clue.text: One picks voters closer to the front

indicators.note: the closer, the word's final letter, is brought round to the front

parts.note: the people who vote are its electors

explanation.surface: A selector chooses which voters get nearer the front of the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closer' reads as the comparative 'nearer', but it is a noun: the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A selector chooses, for instance picking players for a team.

clue.text: Book of sorcery forbidding passion, suppressing love

indicators.note: the outer words hold love down inside them

parts.note: a forbidding look is grim
ire is anger, an intense passion

explanation.surface: A spell book bans passion and stifles love.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O, nil in tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimoire is a textbook of magic, giving spells and instructions for summoning spirits.

clue.text: Second film director to take on this gem of a novel

indicators.note: the director takes the word on before him in the charade

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second
taken as written, the word the director takes before him
Oliver Stone directed Platoon and JFK

explanation.surface: A second-unit film director agrees to adapt this treasured novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Moonstone, by Wilkie Collins, is often called the first English detective novel; the gem is its stolen diamond.
explanation.definitionFit: A moonstone is a pearly gemstone, and The Moonstone is a Victorian novel named after one.

clue.text: The spirit of Lillie Langtry

indicators.note: of here means taken out of the name, which holds the answer within it

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two names

explanation.surface: A tribute to the vivacious character of the Victorian actress Lillie Langtry.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is flair and vigour, a lively spirit.

clue.text: Played guitar with odd characters in Giza's pyramidal tower

indicators.note: a guitar that is played makes a new arrangement of sounds, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first, third and fifth characters of the word are taken

parts.note: the Egyptian city's name, whose first and third letters are the odd ones

explanation.surface: Someone strums a guitar among the odd sorts beside the pyramids at Giza.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pyramidal tower' tempts towards Egypt; a ziggurat is a stepped Mesopotamian temple tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A ziggurat is a terraced pyramid-shaped temple tower of ancient Mesopotamia.

clue.text: Axe clamp used in The Godfather

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a clamp across a guitar's neck that raises the pitch; axe is slang for guitar
second meaning: a Mafia boss, the head of a crime family

explanation.walkthrough: 'Axe' is musicians' slang for a guitar; the clamp bars all strings at one fret.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian word for head names both the guitarist's fret bar and a Mafia chief.

clue.text: Half-hearted friend stifles expression of contempt in an asinine imitative way

indicators.note: the friend smothers the expression, holding it inside
the friend loses half its heart, one of the two central letters

parts.note: an ally is a friend
pish is an exclamation of scorn

explanation.surface: A lukewarm friend swallows a scornful remark while behaving like a silly copycat.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting apishly means mimicking like a monkey, foolishly copying others.

clue.text: High priest from Asia cavorting with chap

indicators.note: jumping about wildly, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A senior cleric from the East dances about with a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Caiaphas was the Jewish high priest who presided over the trial of Jesus.

clue.text: A feature of bridge, though missing 6, is standing

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the bridge feature lacks a piece, which is removed

parts.note: bidding is the auction phase of the card game bridge
6 down's answer is middle: the middle letter of the bridge word is lost

explanation.surface: A bridge's structural part, though its centre has gone, is still standing.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' points to the answer at 6 down, the word middle, so the bridge feature loses its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abiding is enduring or long-standing, as in an abiding friendship.

clue.text: Cook given French kiss after promoting recipe

indicators.note: the recipe's letter is promoted from the tail of the French verb to a higher place in it

parts.note: baiser is French for to kiss; baise is its form
R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on a prescription

explanation.surface: A chef receives a French kiss after recommending a recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French kiss' is the French verb, not a passionate kiss; its last letter moves up near the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To braise is to cook slowly in a little liquid in a covered pot.

clue.text: He painted Jimmy at school naked

parts.note: jimmy riddle is rhyming slang for piddle, so a jimmy is a pee

indicators.note: stripped of its outer covering, the school loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: An artist painted a boy called Jimmy at school without clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Jimmy riddle is British rhyming slang for piddle, so 'Jimmy' means urine; Harrow is an elite boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Camille Pissarro was a French Impressionist painter.

clue.text: Decline to return books reminiscent of the Naughty Nineties

indicators.note: the word turns back on itself, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: to sag is to droop or decline
lit is short for literature

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to give back library books evoking the 1890s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline to return' looks like refusing to give back; 'decline' is the word that is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Streets of the 1890s were lit by gas lamps, so the word evokes that era's atmosphere.

clue.text: One upstanding young lady's stocking fibre

indicators.note: the young lady stocks, or holds, the one inside
in a down clue standing up means read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: a lass is a young woman; the 's is the link to the next word
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An upright young woman's stocking is made of a particular fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stocking' looks like hosiery, but it means containing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a stiff plant fibre from an agave, used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Cleric performing with horn and recorder

indicators.note: putting on a show, so the letters are put through new moves

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A churchman plays music on a horn and a recorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recorder' looks like the instrument in this musical scene; it is someone who records history.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicler writes a historical record of events, a recorder of history.

clue.text: Slew small goat

parts.note: a kid is a young goat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Slew' looks like the past of slay; here it is a verb meaning to slide sideways.
explanation.definitionFit: A car that slews out of control slides sideways across the road.

clue.text: Astronomer Royal entertained by Jerry Lewis

indicators.note: the comedian hosts the astronomer, who is held within his name

parts.note: the letters span the join between the two names

explanation.surface: A senior scientist is amused by the slapstick of comedian Jerry Lewis.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Martin Ryle, radio astronomy pioneer and Nobel laureate, held the post of Astronomer Royal from 1972.

clue.text: The old revolutionary, full of pain, closed diary in Carter's study

indicators.note: the reversed word is filled with the following pieces
turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
gyp is British slang for pain, as in 'my knee is giving me gyp'
a door pushed to is closed
a log is a daily record

explanation.surface: An aged rebel in agony shuts his diary on the subject Carter studied.
explanation.walkthrough: Howard Carter discovered Tutankhamun's tomb; 'closed' is TO as in pulling a door to.
explanation.definitionFit: Egyptology, the study of ancient Egypt, was the field of the archaeologist Howard Carter.
